title: Investigatio motuum, quibus laminae et virgae elasticae contremiscunt

deep.reconstruction:
This page finishes Euler's classification of the end conditions for the transverse vibrations of an elastic rod EF of length a. The rod obeys the Euler–Bernoulli beam equation, with bending stiffness written b c^4.

On the previous page, Case I (free end) gave y'' = 0 (no bending moment) and y''' = 0 (no shear force) at s = 0.

Case II, end 'simpliciter fixus' (pinned, held by a pin about which it turns freely): y = 0, and the first of the §8 equations (moment) gives y'' = 0. The second equation (shear) no longer imposes a condition. It only determines the reaction force F = b c^4 y''' at the pin. Euler remarks that this force does not matter because it does not enter the vibratory motion. Two conditions: y = 0, y'' = 0.

Case III, end 'infixus' (clamped, built into a wall): y = 0 and y' = 0, since the tangent must coincide with the axis. Two conditions.

Each end supplies two conditions, so the two ends E (s = 0) and F (s = a) together give four homogeneous linear equations. Their unknowns are the constants α, β, γ, δ of the general solution y = α e^{s/f} + β e^{-s/f} + γ sin(s/f) + δ cos(s/f). The four equations fix the ratios of the constants. Setting their determinant to zero gives the frequency equation for f, and hence the length k of the isochronous simple pendulum.

Scholion 2 (§14) notes that three conditions per end give 9 combinations. Because the ends can be interchanged, only 6 are distinct: free–free, free–pinned, free–clamped, pinned–pinned, pinned–clamped, clamped–clamped. These six are listed on the next page. In effect this is a short catalogue of boundary conditions for a fourth-order eigenvalue problem.
errors: None of substance. The sign of the shear reaction F = ±b c^4 y''' depends on orientation conventions; it is immaterial here.

Implicit gap: Euler does not discuss whether the four conditions always give a nontrivial determinant equation with real roots. This is standard and later justified by Sturm–Liouville-type self-adjointness.

ideas.what: Boundary conditions for free, pinned and clamped beam ends: (y''=0, y'''=0), (y=0, y''=0), (y=0, y'=0)
ideas.modern_name: Euler–Bernoulli beam boundary conditions (free, simply supported, clamped)
ideas.where_published: E65, Additamentum I de curvis elasticis (1744); E40; E526 itself; discussed in Truesdell, Rational Mechanics of Flexible or Elastic Bodies (1960)

ideas.what: Reaction force at a pinned support is determined by y''' but does not affect the vibration
ideas.modern_name: Reaction from the shear-force boundary term (natural vs essential boundary conditions)

ideas.what: Enumeration of the six distinct combinations of end conditions, with four conditions giving the constants and a frequency equation
ideas.modern_name: Classical beam eigenvalue problems / frequency (characteristic) equations

deep.surprise_reason: This is a standard, well-documented classification of beam end conditions, already present in Euler's 1744 work and covered by Truesdell. Nothing here is new.
transcription_corrections: Next page: '(d^3 s/ds^3)=0' should read '(d^3 y/ds^3)=0'.
